transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I suppose what brought me in is that I’m having trouble with eating, more than I’d like to admit. It’s embarrassing to say at my age, but sometimes once I start, it feels like my hands just keep reaching for more, even when I’m telling myself, “Tom, stop this right now.” I don’t seem to listen to myself in those moments. Is that… the sort of thing you need to know?
Can you describe what happens during these times when you feel like you can’t stop eating? Are there times when you eat a lot in a short period, more than most people would in similar circumstances?

Yes… I think so. I don’t like how it sounds, but yes.

It tends to be when I’m alone at the house in the afternoon. I’ll tell myself I’m just having a sandwich or a little something, and then it sort of gets away from me. I can go through bread with peanut butter, then cookies, maybe leftovers from the fridge, and ice cream too… all in one sitting, before I really even stop and notice what I’ve done.

I know that’s probably more than most people would eat. It’s not every meal or anything, but when it happens, it’s a lot. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
During these times when you keep eating even though you tell yourself to stop, do you feel like you’re not in control of what or how much you’re eating?

Yes… I suppose I do. I don’t like admitting that, but what scares me most is that once I start eating, it’s like my hands just keep reaching for more, even while I’m telling myself, “Tom, stop this right now.”

It’s not that I don’t know I should stop. I do know. I just… don’t seem to be the one in charge right then, if that makes sense.
After these episodes of eating more than you intend to, do you ever try to make up for it by doing things like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot more than usual?

I… yes. I’m ashamed to say it, but there are times after I’ve eaten too much when I go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up.

Not every time, but… enough that I know it’s not right. And I’ve taken laxatives too, because I get frightened the food will just stay in me. I know that probably sounds awful. Is it okay that I’m telling you this plainly?

latest_inference.note: This turn confirmed compensatory behaviors such as self-induced vomiting and laxative use following episodes of overeating, which aligns with the diagnostic criteria for Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2).
